text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesdau. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- Parliament voted to withdraw the parliamentary immunity of deputy Valdis Krisbergs and allowed criminal proceedings to start against him.
- The court of the city of Daugavpils has declined the application of the general prosecutor's office for the mandate of city mayor, Alexei Vidavski, to be cancelled.
- The minister of culture, Rihards Piks, has met musicians and artists of the national opera who threatened to strike unless their salaries were not increased.
- Prime Minister Shkele announced at a meeting with German bankers that leaving the Baltic states outside the security zone could lead to a new conflict between the East and West.
DIENA
- Latvian Development Agency opens its office in Frankfurt.
- Latvia has restored its right to vote in the U.N. after paying off about a half of its debt, which amounts four million.
- The chief notary of the company register Maris Gulbis believes the security police should not interfere with the process of registering foreign companies offices in Latvia.
NEATKARIGA RITA AVIZE
- WEU Secretary-General, Jose Cutillero, is due on a two-day official visit to Latvia tomorrow.
- Representatives of Latvia, Estonia and Sweden have initialled an agreement on the common maritime border points in the Baltic Sea.
- An American-registered company, Crosstrade Inc. Latvia LTD, has become the owner of VNA, the TV company broadcasting on the 31st channel.
BIZNES & BALTIYA
- Parliament voted to set up a committee to investigate the legitimacy of the privatization of Savings bank and Unibanka. Its final report is due to be submitted by May 1.
- The prosecutor's office says Alexander Lavent could be released on bail of 1 million lats.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs comments on the results of the Helsinki summit and Yeltsin's yesterday's statement regarding security guarantees to the Baltic States. Latvia declines any unilateral or multilateral guarantees as it sees its participation in NATO as the only guarantor to its security.
SM
- Parliament votes to abolish the provision of the law on ports requiring that a port chief manager is to have higher maritime education.
DIENAS BIZNESS

- The amendments to a on Gambling, passed yesterday, which ban gambling coffee shops, restaurants and other public places and prohibits running gambling houses in cellars may result in a loss of half a million lats for the state budget.
